subject: First residency measurement of the Gravity runtime, on the freshly sealed Math-Preserve artifact, with the bounded GPU weight cache live
why_this_could_not_be_measured_before: The cache was unbounded and had no accounting, so nobody could say how much the runtime was holding. Gap G1 had to close before G2 could be asked.

residency.reading: Twelve decode tokens at context 4 pulled 8,818 tensors and 22.0 GB resident -- roughly 1.8 GB of NEW device residency per token. The bound was never hit, so zero evictions, but the trajectory is the point: at this rate the 32 GiB budget binds at around token 18, and an UNBOUNDED cache reaches the whole 92 GB artifact within a few tens of tokens on a 96 GiB host shared with other work.
residency.verdict: The unbounded cache was not a theoretical risk. This is the measurement that shows it, and it is why BASE_TRUE_TPS had only ever been taken over twelve tokens.

honest_reading_of_the_tps.still_cold: Both arms remain COLD-START numbers. Every one of the twelve tokens is paying first-touch disk read, hash verification and device upload for essentially every expert it routes to -- 1.8 GB of new residency per token proves there is no steady state anywhere in this window.
honest_reading_of_the_tps.the_bound_did_not_make_it_faster: 0.1487 and 0.1506 tok/s against 0.157 previously measured on General-R0. Within noise. Exactly as predicted when the cache work was reviewed: bounding residency is about not exhausting memory, not about throughput. Reporting it as a speedup would have been dishonest.
honest_reading_of_the_tps.context_barely_moves_decode: Decode is flat from ctx 4 to ctx 128 (6756 vs 6628 ms/token median) while prefill grows 14x (56.6 s to 806.8 s). Decode cost here is dominated by expert residency traffic, not by attention over context.
honest_reading_of_the_tps.warm_still_unmeasured: A genuine warm number needs a run long enough for the routed working set to saturate, which by this measurement means well past the budget and into steady-state eviction. That run has not been done.

what_this_changes: BASE_TRUE_TPS can now be stated with its residency alongside it, which it never could before. The scoreboard entry should carry resident bytes and eviction count next to the token rate, because on a routed MoE a throughput number without a residency number is uninterpretable.
next: Run long enough to cross the budget and measure steady-state decode with eviction active. That is the first honest warm number and the first test of the LRU under real routing rather than unit tests.
not_evidence_of: warm or steady-state throughput, or any acceleration
